ui.noResults: Nothing in Help matches “{{query}}”. Try other words, or browse the contents.

welcome.title: Welcome to {{app}}
welcome.summary: A free PDF viewer and editor for engineers that works in your browser, offline. Your documents never leave this device.

body.alt: The {{app}} window with a drawing open, numbered from 1 to 6
body.caption: 1 Top bar · 2 Ribbon · 3 Side panes · 4 Document · 5 Properties pane · 6 Status bar

steps: The top bar has the quick commands (Open, Save, Print, Undo, Redo), your open documents as tabs, the dark theme switch, full screen and the links to OpenEngTools and GitHub.
The ribbon has the commands, grouped in tabs: File, Home, View, Comment, Form, Measure, Organize, Convert, Protect and Help. Point at any button to see its name and shortcut.
The side panes on the left show thumbnails, bookmarks, attachments, layers, signatures, comments and search results.
The document area shows the pages. Scroll, zoom and work on them here.
The Properties pane on the right shows the selected comment, form field or tool, and lets you change it.
The status bar has the page number, the zoom, the view mode, snapping and whether {{app}} is ready offline.

body.tip: Press <kbd>{{help}}</kbd> in {{app}} at any time to open Help at the topic for what you are doing.

list: [Open a PDF](#opening-files), then [zoom and move around](#zoom-and-pages).
[Add comments](#comment-tab) and [review them](#reviewing-comments) with others.
[Measure](#measure-tools) distances and areas on a drawing.
[Fill in or create forms](#filling-forms), [sign](#signing) or [redact](#redaction) a document.

opening-files.title: Opening files
opening-files.summary: Open PDFs from your computer, by drag and drop, or from the list of recent files. Each file opens in its own tab.

body.alt: The start screen with the Open button and the recent files list
body.caption: The start screen: 1 Open a file · 2 Recent files

steps: Press {{open}}, or choose Open on the start screen or in the File tab.
Pick one or more PDF files and choose Open.
Each file opens in its own tab in the top bar. Click a tab to switch documents, or close it with its ×.

list: You can also drag PDF files from your desktop or file manager and drop them on the window.
File › Recent lists the files you opened on this device. Click one to open it again.
A password-protected file asks for its password first. See [Protected and signed files](#protected-files).

body.alt: Two documents open as tabs in the top bar
body.caption: Two documents open as tabs.

body.tip: If {{app}} is installed as an app, you can also open PDFs with it from your file manager (“Open with”).

offline.title: Installing and working offline
offline.summary: {{app}} keeps a copy of itself on this device, so it opens and works without an internet connection.

steps: Open {{app}} once while you are online. It downloads what it needs in the background.
Wait until the status bar shows ✓ Ready offline.
From then on, {{app}} works with no connection, including Help.

body.alt: The status bar showing Ready offline
body.caption: The status bar when {{app}} is ready to work offline.

body.h: To install it as an app

steps: In Chrome or Edge, choose the install icon at the right of the address bar (or the browser menu › Install {{app}}).
{{app}} opens in its own window and appears with your other apps.

body.p: When a new version is ready, the status bar shows Update ready. Choose it to restart with the new version. It never restarts while you have documents open; Help › Check for Updates looks for one now.

home-tab.title: The Home tab
home-tab.summary: The Home tab gathers the commands you use most: tools, zoom, view, comments, measuring and signing.

body.alt: The Home tab of the ribbon, with its groups numbered
body.caption: 1 Tools · 2 Zoom · 3 View · 4 Comment · 5 Measure · 6 Protect

steps: Tools: Hand ({{hand}}) moves the page, Select ({{select}}) picks text and comments, Snapshot copies part of a page as a picture, Find and Advanced Search find text.
Zoom: zoom in and out, fit the page or its width, or show it at its actual size.
View: rotate the view, and open the Comments, Thumbnails, Bookmarks and Attachments panes or the Properties pane.
Comment: the comment tools you use most.
Measure: distance, perimeter and area.
Protect: Sign Document.

body.tip: The Tools and View groups show icons only. Point at an icon, or move to it with <kbd>Tab</kbd>, to see its name and shortcut. On a narrow window, groups first lose their labels and then fold into menus.

zoom-and-pages.title: Zoom, pages and full screen
zoom-and-pages.summary: Zoom, move between pages, choose how pages are laid out, and show the app full screen.

body.alt: The View tab of the ribbon
body.caption: The View tab: go to a page, zoom, page display and window options.

list: <kbd>{{zoomIn}}</kbd> and <kbd>{{zoomOut}}</kbd>, or hold <kbd>{{mod}}</kbd> and turn the mouse wheel.
<kbd>{{fitPage}}</kbd> fits the whole page, <kbd>{{fitWidth}}</kbd> fits its width and <kbd>{{actualSize}}</kbd> shows it at its actual size.
View › Loupe magnifies the area under the pointer, and Pan and Zoom Window shows where you are on a large drawing.
Scroll, or hold <kbd>Space</kbd> (or press <kbd>{{hand}}</kbd> for the Hand tool) and drag the page.
Type a page number in the status bar, or use the first, previous, next and last page buttons.
View › Single Page, Continuous, Facing and Continuous Facing set how pages are laid out.

body.alt: The status bar with page navigation, view mode and zoom
body.caption: The status bar: 1 Page number · 2 View mode · 3 Zoom

body.p: Home › Rotate View and View › Rotate View turn the pages on screen only; the file does not change. To turn pages in the file itself, see [Organizing pages](#organize-pages).
{{fullScreen}} or the full-screen button at the top right shows the whole app full screen. Esc leaves full screen. View › Collapse Ribbon gives the pages more room.

themes.title: Light and dark themes
themes.summary: Switch between the light and dark look of {{app}}. Pages always stay white.

steps: Click the moon button at the top right, or press <kbd>{{darkTheme}}</kbd>.
The app turns dark. Click the sun button (or press the keys again) to go back to light.

body.alt: {{app}} in the dark theme with a white page
body.caption: The dark theme: the app is dark, the page stays white.

list: View › Dark Theme and File › Settings › Appearance do the same.
Your choice is kept on this device only, and Help follows it.
Form fields, sticky note windows and comment handles keep their light look, so they read well on the white page.
File › Settings › Clear all local data goes back to the light theme.

side-panes.title: Side panes and the Properties pane
side-panes.summary: The rail on the left opens panes for thumbnails, bookmarks, attachments, layers, signatures, comments and search results.

body.alt: The Thumbnails pane open on the left of a document
body.caption: 1 The rail · 2 The Thumbnails pane

steps: Click an icon in the rail to open its pane. Click it again to close the pane.
Drag the pane's edge to make it wider or narrower.
Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> in a pane to go back to the rail.

list: Thumbnails: small pictures of the pages. Click one to go to it; select several to work on them (see [Organizing pages](#organize-pages)).
Bookmarks: the document's outline. See [Bookmarks](#bookmarks).
Attachments: files embedded in the PDF. See [Attaching files](#attaching-files).
Layers: show or hide a drawing's layers.
Signatures: the digital signatures in the file and whether each signed part is unchanged.
Comments: every comment in the document. See [Reviewing comments](#reviewing-comments).
Search Results: the results of Advanced Search.

body.p: The Properties pane on the right (Home › Properties Pane) shows the selected comment, form field or tool. See [Comment properties](#comment-properties).

finding-text.title: Finding text
finding-text.summary: Find words on the pages with Quick Find, or search comments, bookmarks and other open documents with Advanced Search.

body.h: To find text in the document

steps: Press {{find}} (or Home › Find).
Type the words and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>. {{app}} searches only when you press Enter.
Press <kbd>{{findNext}}</kbd> or <kbd>Enter</kbd> again for the next match. Every match is marked on the pages.

body.alt: The Find bar with matches highlighted on the page
body.caption: Quick Find: the current match is orange, the others yellow.

steps: Press {{advancedSearch}} (or Home › Advanced Search).
Type the words, choose where to look (the pages, comments, bookmarks, this document or every open document) and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>.
Click a result in the Search Results pane to go to it.

body.alt: The Search Results pane listing matches with their page numbers

body.tip: A scanned page has no text to find until you run [OCR](#ocr) on it.

bookmarks.title: Bookmarks
bookmarks.summary: Bookmarks are the document's table of contents. Use them to jump around, and add, rename, move and style them.

body.alt: The Bookmarks pane with nested bookmarks and its toolbar
body.caption: The Bookmarks pane: 1 Toolbar · 2 Bookmarks

steps: Go to the page, and zoom, that the bookmark should open.
In the Bookmarks pane, choose New Bookmark (or press Insert).
Type its title and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>.

list: Rename: select it and press <kbd>F2</kbd>.
Move: drag it, or use <kbd>Alt+Shift</kbd> with the arrow keys. Drop it on another bookmark to put it inside.
Delete: press <kbd>{{delete}}</kbd>.
Right-click a bookmark (or press <kbd>{{menu}}</kbd>) for New Child Bookmark, Cut, Copy, Paste, Set Destination, Expand All and Collapse All.

body.alt: The right-click menu of a bookmark
body.caption: The bookmark menu.

body.p: Bookmark Properties (Alt+Enter) sets the title, colour, bold, italic, page and zoom. Every change is one undo step, and {{save}} saves them in the file.

body.tip: A file that does not allow changes keeps its bookmarks as they are.

comment-tab.title: Adding comments
comment-tab.summary: The Comment tab has every markup tool: text markup, notes, text boxes, shapes, stamps and more.

body.alt: The Comment tab of the ribbon, with its groups numbered
body.caption: 1 Tools · 2 Text · 3 Note · 4 Text markup · 5 Drawing · 6 Stamp · 7 Measure · 8 Manage comments

steps: Open the Comment tab and choose a tool, for example Rectangle.
Drag on the page to draw it (or click, for notes and stamps).
The new comment stays selected, so you can change its look in the Properties pane straight away.
Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to put the tool down.

list: Single letters such as <kbd>N</kbd> (sticky note) or <kbd>B</kbd> (rectangle) choose a tool while the document has focus. Point at a tool to see its letter.
New comments are red with 1 pt lines and 10 pt text. Highlights are yellow at 50 % opacity, sticky notes are yellow, and the typewriter writes in black Courier.
The small arrow beside a tool opens its styles. See [Comment styles](#comment-styles).
<kbd>{{undo}}</kbd> undoes the last change, and <kbd>{{save}}</kbd> keeps your comments in the file.

body.tip: Comments are standard PDF comments: they show in Adobe Acrobat Reader, PDF-XChange and other PDF viewers.

text-markup.title: Highlighting and marking up text
text-markup.summary: Highlight, underline, strike out or squiggle text, or mark where text should be inserted or replaced.

steps: Choose Highlight, Underline, Strikeout or Squiggly on the Comment tab.
Drag across the text on the page.
Release the mouse. The markup is added and stays selected.

body.alt: Text on a page with a yellow highlight, an underline and a strikeout

list: Insert Text marks where text should go, and Replace Text strikes text out and marks the replacement.
Highlight Area highlights a rectangle, for drawings with no text. Free Highlight highlights freehand.
You can also select text first with Select, then right-click it and choose a markup.

text-comments.title: Text boxes, typewriters and callouts
text-comments.summary: Put text on the page: in a box, as plain typed text, or in a box with a leader line that points at something.

steps: Choose Callout on the Comment tab.
Press on the point the callout marks and drag to where its text box should go.
Type the text. “Type here” is selected, so typing replaces it.
Click elsewhere, or press <kbd>Esc</kbd>, to keep your text.

body.alt: A callout pointing at part of a drawing, with its text box
body.caption: A callout: 1 the point it marks · 2 the text box

body.p: Text Box and Typewriter work the same way: drag a box (or click), then type. A typewriter has no border and its lines do not wrap.

list: Click a text comment to select it, and drag it to move it.
Double-click it to edit the text with the caret where you clicked, or select it and press <kbd>Enter</kbd> or <kbd>{{editText}}</kbd>.
While editing, right-click the text for Undo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Select All, Text Style and Properties.
Text boxes and callouts grow taller as you type more lines, so nothing is cut off.

body.alt: The right-click menu while editing a text box, with Text Style
body.caption: The text menu while you edit.

body.tip: Text Style and the Properties pane change the whole comment: font, size, bold, italic, colour and alignment. A text box and a callout have a Text color and a Border color of their own.

sticky-notes.title: Sticky notes
sticky-notes.summary: A sticky note is a small icon on the page with a note window for longer comments and replies.

steps: Choose Sticky Note on the Comment tab (or press N).
Click on the page. The note window opens.
Type your note. <kbd>Enter</kbd> starts a new line.
Click elsewhere or press <kbd>{{mod}}+Enter</kbd> to keep the text; <kbd>Esc</kbd> keeps it and closes the window.

body.alt: A sticky note icon with its open note window
body.caption: A sticky note and its window: 1 menu · 2 Lock · 3 Reply

list: Drag the window's title bar to move it, and its corner to resize it.
Its ⋮ menu sets the status, deletes the note or opens Properties.
Double-click a note (or select it and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>) to open its window again. Several can be open at once.
<kbd>{{save}}</kbd> keeps where each window is and whether it is open.

shapes.title: Shapes, lines and drawing
shapes.summary: Draw rectangles, ovals, clouds, lines, arrows, polylines, polygons and freehand pen strokes.

steps: Choose a shape on the Comment tab, for example Cloud.
Drag on the page. For a polyline, polygon or cloud, click each corner and double-click (or press <kbd>Enter</kbd>) to finish.
Change the colour, line width or fill in the Properties pane.

body.alt: A red rectangle, a cloud and an arrow drawn on a drawing

list: Hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> while you drag for a square, a circle, or a line at 45° steps.
Pencil draws freehand. Free Highlight draws a wide, see-through stroke.
Drag a selected shape's handles to resize it. A hollow shape is selected by clicking its border.

stamps.title: Stamps
stamps.summary: Put a status stamp (for example Approved or For Comment) or a picture on the page.

steps: Choose Stamp on the Comment tab.
Pick the status code, and type the document number and revision if you want them on the stamp.
Choose Place stamp, then click on the page (or press Enter to place it in the middle of the page).

body.alt: The Stamp dialog with a status code, document number and revision

list: The stamp shows the code, your name, today's date, and the document's number and revision.
Status Schemes sets which codes you can choose from, for your project's own review process.
Image Stamp places a PNG or JPG picture, or the first page of a PDF.

selecting-comments.title: Selecting, moving and deleting comments
selecting-comments.summary: Select one comment or many, then move, nudge, copy or delete them together.

list: Click a comment with Select ({{select}}) or Select Comments to select it.
Drag a rectangle on the page to select every comment it touches. With Select, start the drag beside the text.
<kbd>Shift</kbd>+click or <kbd>{{mod}}</kbd>+click adds a comment to the selection or takes it out.
{{selectAll}} with Select Comments selects every comment on the page.

body.alt: Three comments selected together after dragging a rectangle around them

list: Drag them, or nudge them with the arrow keys (<kbd>Shift</kbd> for bigger steps).
Press <kbd>{{delete}}</kbd> to delete them, and <kbd>{{undo}}</kbd> to bring them back.
Right-click for Copy, Cut, Paste, Flatten, Locked, Printable and Properties.

body.tip: A locked comment can't be moved or changed until you clear Locked in its menu or the Properties pane.

comment-properties.title: Comment properties and colours
comment-properties.summary: The Properties pane shows every property of the selected comment, and changes it.

body.alt: The Properties pane for a selected rectangle
body.caption: The Properties pane: 1 General · 2 Style

steps: Select a comment.
Open the Properties pane (Home › Properties Pane) if it is not open.
Change a property. The comment changes at once, and each change is one undo step.

list: General: subject, author, dates, Printable, Read only, Locked, Marked and the review history.
Style: fill and stroke colour, line style and width, opacity, blend mode and rotation.
Text: font, size, bold, italic and alignment.

steps: Click a colour box.
Click a colour in Standard colors (or move with the arrow keys and press Enter).
More colors… opens your system's colour picker. Fill colours also offer No fill.

body.alt: The Standard colors picker opened from a colour box

body.tip: Right-click a comment and choose Make Current Properties Default to draw the next ones like it.

comment-styles.title: Comment styles
comment-styles.summary: Save named looks for each comment tool and switch between them in one click.

steps: Choose Comment › Comment Styles (or Comment Styles Palette… under a tool's arrow).
Pick a tool on the left.
Select a style, or Clone one to make your own, and change its properties on the right.
Choose Set Current to draw the tool's next comments in that style.

body.alt: The Comment Styles Palette window
body.caption: 1 Tools · 2 Current Style and Custom Styles · 3 Properties

list: Rename, Reset and Delete are on the toolbar. Reset brings a preset back.
Reset All puts every tool back to its default and restores the presets. Your own styles are kept.
Export… and Import… share styles with colleagues as a file.
On the ribbon, the arrow beside a tool lists its styles too.

reviewing-comments.title: Reviewing comments
reviewing-comments.summary: The Comments pane lists every comment, with replies, statuses, filters and search.

body.alt: The Comments pane with comment cards, a reply and a status
body.caption: The Comments pane: 1 Find · 2 A comment card

steps: Open the Comments pane (Home › Comments, or the rail).
On the comment's card, choose Reply.
Type your reply and press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to post it (<kbd>Esc</kbd> cancels).

body.p: Right-click the comment (on the page or its card) › Set Status, and choose Accepted, Rejected, Cancelled, Completed or your own scheme's statuses. The card shows the status and who set it.

list: Options sorts, groups and filters the cards by page, author, type or status.
Find (press Enter) looks through the comments' text and replies.
Click a card to go to its comment. <kbd>F2</kbd> edits its text.
Comment › Export CRS (Excel) builds a comment resolution sheet.

flatten-snapshot.title: Flattening comments and snapshots
flatten-snapshot.summary: Make comments part of the page, or copy part of a page as a picture.

steps: Choose Comment › Flatten Comments.
Choose the selected comments, or all comments on some pages.
Choose Flatten. The comments are drawn into the page: they print and show everywhere, but can no longer be edited.

body.alt: The Flatten Comments dialog

list: Locked and hidden comments, links and redaction marks are left as they are.
<kbd>{{undo}}</kbd> brings the comments back until you save.

steps: Choose Home › Snapshot.
Drag a rectangle on the page.
The area is copied to the clipboard as a picture. Paste it into an e-mail, a report or another app.

body.tip: From the keyboard, the arrow keys move and resize the snapshot rectangle and <kbd>Enter</kbd> copies it. A document that does not allow copying refuses snapshots.

comment-transfer.title: Copying, exporting and importing comments
comment-transfer.summary: Move comments between documents, or save them as CSV, Excel or JSON and bring them back.

body.h: To copy comments to another document

steps: Select the comments and press <kbd>{{copy}}</kbd> (or <kbd>{{cut}}</kbd>).
Go to the other document (or another page) and click the page.
Press {{paste}}. They go on the page you clicked, at the same place. Paste to Original Pages puts them on the pages they came from.
Choose Comment › Export Comments.
Choose CSV or Excel for a list you can read and filter, or JSON to keep the comments exactly as they are.
Choose the pages, authors, types and statuses, then Export.
Choose Comment › Import Comments.
Pick another PDF or a {{app}} JSON export.
Choose which comments to bring in, and Import.

body.alt: The Import Comments dialog with its options

body.tip: A JSON export keeps everything: the look, replies, statuses, stamps, pictures, attached files and sticky note windows. Importing it brings the same comments back.

pasting-pictures.title: Pasting pictures
pasting-pictures.summary: Paste a screenshot or an image you copied in another app onto the page.

steps: Copy a picture: take a screenshot, or copy an image in another app.
Click the page in {{app}}.
Press {{paste}}, or right-click the page and choose Paste.

body.alt: A pasted screenshot on the page, selected
body.caption: The picture is placed as an image stamp, scaled to fit the page, and selected.

list: The newest thing you copied is pasted: the picture or the comments.
Paste from the menu may ask once to allow clipboard access.
Pictures up to 20 MB are accepted; other formats are converted to PNG.

attaching-files.title: Attaching files
attaching-files.summary: Put a file on the page as a paperclip comment, or see the files embedded in the PDF.

steps: Choose Comment › Attach File.
Click on the page, and pick the file (up to 25 MB).
A paperclip shows where it is. Double-click it to save the file.

body.alt: The Attachments pane listing a file attached to the document

body.p: The Attachments pane lists every file in the PDF, attached to a page or to the whole document. Choose one to open it or save it.

measure-scale.title: Setting the scale
measure-scale.summary: Tell {{app}} the drawing's scale, so measurements show real lengths and areas.

steps: Choose Measure › Set Scale.
Type the paper length and the real length (for example 1 mm = 100 mm) and choose the units.
Choose which pages it applies to, and Apply.

body.alt: The Set scale dialog

steps: Choose Measure › Calibrate.
Click two points a known distance apart, for example the ends of a dimension line.
Type that distance and choose Apply.

list: Scale Viewport gives part of a page its own scale, for a sheet with details at another scale.
Units and Precision sets the units, decimal places and rounding.

measure-tools.title: Measuring distance, perimeter and area
measure-tools.summary: Measure on the page. Each measurement is a comment with its value, saved in the file.

body.alt: The Measure tab of the ribbon
body.caption: 1 Measure tools · 2 Scale · 3 Snapping

steps: Set the scale first (see [Setting the scale](#measure-scale)).
Choose Distance, Perimeter or Area on the Measure tab.
For Distance, drag from one point to the other. For Perimeter and Area, click each corner and double-click (or press <kbd>Enter</kbd>) to finish.
The value shows on the page and in the Properties pane.

body.alt: A distance and an area measured on a drawing, with their values

body.tip: Measurements are comments, so they appear in the Comments pane and can be exported with the other comments.

snapping.title: Snapping
snapping.summary: Snap measurement and drawing points exactly to the drawing's lines.

steps: Turn snapping on with the magnet in the status bar, or Measure › Enable Snapping.
Choose what to snap to on the Measure tab: endpoints, midpoints, intersections and nearest point on a line.
Move the pointer near the drawing. A marker shows the point it will snap to.

body.alt: The snapping options on the Measure tab

filling-forms.title: Filling in forms
filling-forms.summary: Type in a PDF form's fields, tick its boxes and choose its options, then save.

steps: Click a form field, or press <kbd>Tab</kbd> to move from field to field.
Type, tick or choose the value.
Press <kbd>{{save}}</kbd> to save the values in the file.

body.alt: A form with its fields tinted by Highlight Fields
body.caption: Highlight Fields tints the fields so you can see them.

list: Form › Highlight Fields shows or hides the tint.
Form › Reset Form puts every field back to its default.
A file that does not allow form filling keeps its fields read-only.

creating-fields.title: Creating form fields
creating-fields.summary: Add text fields, check boxes, radio buttons, list boxes and dropdowns to any PDF.

body.alt: The Form tab of the ribbon

steps: Open the Form tab and choose a field type, for example Text Field.
Drag a box on the page (or click for the default size).
Set the field's name, tooltip, default value and look in the Properties pane.

body.alt: The Properties pane of a new text field

list: Radio buttons drawn one after another form one group: only one of them can be on.
For a list box or dropdown, add its items in the Properties pane.
{{app}} never adds scripts to a form.

field-order.title: Editing fields and tab order
field-order.summary: Move, resize and delete fields, and set the order Tab moves through them.

steps: Choose Form › Select Fields.
Click a field to select it. Drag it or its handles to move or resize it; <kbd>{{delete}}</kbd> deletes it.
Click the page away from any field: the Properties pane shows the page's tab order. Move fields up or down in the list.

body.alt: Select Fields with the page's tab order in the Properties pane

organize-pages.title: Organizing pages
organize-pages.summary: Insert, delete, move, extract, rotate and merge pages. These change the file itself.

body.alt: The Organize tab of the ribbon

steps: Select the pages: click thumbnails in the Thumbnails pane (<kbd>Shift</kbd> or <kbd>{{mod}}</kbd>+click for several), or stay on the current page.
Choose a command on the Organize tab: Rotate, Delete Pages, Move Pages, Extract Pages, Insert Blank Page, Insert from File or Merge Files.
Check the result, then press <kbd>{{save}}</kbd>. <kbd>{{undo}}</kbd> undoes a page change.

body.alt: Selected pages in the Thumbnails pane

list: Drag thumbnails to move pages.
Right-click a thumbnail for Cut, Copy and Paste of pages, also between documents.
Extract Pages saves the chosen pages as a new PDF.

body.tip: Rotate on the Organize tab turns the pages in the file. Rotate View on the Home and View tabs turns them on screen only.

export-documents.title: Converting to Word, text and images
export-documents.summary: Save the document's content as Word, text, Markdown, HTML or images, on this device.

body.alt: The Convert tab of the ribbon

steps: Choose a format on the Convert tab: To Word (Beta), To Text, To Markdown, To HTML or Export Images.
Choose the pages and the options.
Choose Export and where to save the file.

body.tip: Conversion runs on this device. Nothing is uploaded. Scanned pages need [OCR](#ocr) first to have text.

extract-tables.title: Extracting tables
extract-tables.summary: Save tables from the pages as an Excel workbook or CSV files.

steps: Choose Convert › Express Extract.
Choose Find Tables, then the format (Excel or CSV).
Choose Save….
Choose Convert › Review & Extract. The tables found are outlined on the page.
Add, move or delete row and column dividers, mark header rows and merge cells.
Save the result, or save the grid as a template for similar pages.

body.alt: Review and Extract showing a table's grid on the page

ocr.title: Recognizing text in scanned pages (OCR)
ocr.summary: Give scanned pages an invisible text layer, so their text can be found, selected and copied.

steps: Choose Convert › Recognize Text (OCR).
Choose the pages and the language.
Choose Recognize. When it finishes, press {{save}}.

body.alt: The Recognize Text (OCR) dialog

list: Recognition runs on this device. Nothing is sent anywhere.
Pages that already have text are skipped unless you choose otherwise.
English is ready offline; other languages download the first time you use them.

redaction.title: Redacting
redaction.summary: Remove sensitive text, images and drawings for good, in a new file.

steps: Select text and choose Protect › Mark for Redaction, or choose Mark Area for Redaction and drag a rectangle.
Check the marks in Pending Redactions. Remove any you don't want.
Choose Apply Redactions and where to save the new file.

body.alt: Redaction marks on a page and the Pending Redactions list
body.caption: Marks wait until you apply them, and can be saved with the document.

body.p: Applying writes a new, fully rewritten file: the marked content is removed, the document's hidden data is cleared, and the file is checked before it is saved. The original file is not changed.

body.tip: Open the redacted file and check it before you share it.

passwords.title: Passwords and permissions
passwords.summary: Protect a copy of the document with a password, limit what others can do with it, or remove protection.

steps: Choose Protect › Password Security….
Set an open password (needed to open the file), a permissions password with what is allowed (printing, copying, changes), or both.
Choose Save and where to save the protected copy. It uses AES-256.

body.alt: The Password Security dialog

list: Remove Security saves a copy without passwords.
Both need the owner (permissions) password of a file that is already protected.
Security Info shows what the open file allows.

signing.title: Signing with your signature
signing.summary: Place your signature or initials on the page: drawn, typed or from a picture.

steps: Choose Protect › Sign Document… (also on the Home tab).
Draw your signature, type your name, or choose a picture of it. Add initials if you want.
Choose Place Signature (or Place Initials), then click on the page. Enter puts it in the middle of the page.

body.alt: The Sign Document dialog with a drawn signature

list: Your signatures are saved on this device, for next time.
The signature is a standard comment. Flatten it to make it part of the page.

body.tip: This is a visual signature, not a certificate-based digital signature: it shows your signature but does not prove who signed or that the file is unchanged.

protected-files.title: Protected and signed files
protected-files.summary: {{app}} respects what a protected file allows, and checks digital signatures.

list: A file with an open password asks for it when you open it.
A file with restrictions shows which commands are not allowed. Protect › Security Info lists what is allowed.
If you have the owner password, Unlock with Owner Password lifts the restrictions for this session.

body.alt: The Security info dialog listing what the file allows

body.p: The Signatures pane lists the file's digital signatures and whether each signed part is unchanged. {{save}} adds your changes after the signed part, so earlier signatures stay intact.

saving.title: Saving
saving.summary: Save changes into the file, save a copy, or rewrite the file compactly.

body.alt: The File tab with Save, Save As and Save Optimized

list: {{save}} (Save) adds your changes to the end of the file. It is quick, and earlier signed versions are kept as they were.
{{saveAs}} (Save As) saves a copy under a new name or place.
Save Optimized rewrites the file compactly. Digital signatures would no longer be valid.

body.p: File › Document Properties shows the document's title, author, file size and structure.

printing.title: Printing
printing.summary: Print pages with or without comments, at the right size and quality.

steps: Press <kbd>{{print}}</kbd>.
Choose the pages, page size, comments and markups, and the quality (High for drawings).
Choose Print, then your printer in the browser's print dialog.

body.alt: The Print dialog

list: Large drawings print sharpest through the browser's PDF viewer, which the dialog offers.
File › Export Print-Ready PDF saves a copy with comments and form values made part of the pages.

recovery.title: Recovering unsaved work
recovery.summary: If the browser closes before you save, {{app}} offers your changes back the next time it starts.

steps: Start {{app}} again.
The Recover unsaved changes? dialog lists the documents with unsaved changes.
Choose Recover to continue where you left off, or Discard.

body.alt: The Recover unsaved changes dialog

body.p: Recovery copies are kept on this device only, never in your original file. They are deleted when you save or discard.

keyboard-shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
keyboard-shortcuts.summary: Every keyboard shortcut in {{app}}, for this computer. Help › Keyboard Shortcuts in the app shows the same list, ready to print.

body.p: Single-letter keys, such as <kbd>{{hand}}</kbd> for Hand, work while the document has focus. Keys marked as reserved by the browser work in the installed app; use the other key shown in a browser tab.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.summary: Your documents never leave this device.

list: {{app}} opens, shows and saves documents in your browser. Nothing is uploaded.
No account, no cookies, no tracking and no analytics.
On its own, {{app}} only loads its program files and checks for updates from its own website.
Error reports are sent only when you choose to, and you see every word first.

body.alt: The Privacy page in the File tab

body.p: File › Privacy lists everything {{app}} keeps on this device. File › Settings › Clear all local data deletes it.

reporting-problems.title: Reporting a problem
reporting-problems.summary: Tell us what went wrong, by an error report or on GitHub. Never attach confidential documents.

steps: In {{app}}, choose Help › Send Error Report.
Describe what you were doing (optional). Don't paste text from your documents.
Read the report exactly as it will be sent, then choose Send.

body.alt: The Send Error Report dialog

body.p: The report never contains your documents, their names or their text. Offline, you can copy it and send it later.
The GitHub button at the top right of {{app}} opens a new issue with the app version, browser and operating system filled in.
